data.name: Baobabs Mausoleum Ep.2: 1313 Barnabas Dead End Drive
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to Flamingos Creek, the ghostly town which only appears each 25 years in Albatros Road. A town that only appears in nightmares!

Now arrives the second Baobabs Mausoleum chapter with “Baobabs Mausoleum Ep.2: 1313 Barnabas Dead End Drive” which follows the adventure of our FBI Agent Watracio Walpurgis in his quest: Escape from Flamingos Creek.

Now you can explore Flamingos Creek wilfully! Mixing David Lynch, Twin Peaks and the Zelda Saga, you will find the logic evolution of an “open town”, where you will have a profound experience with the town, its inhabitants, main story and secondary missions.



Explore the whole town with real cycles of night and day. Explore Flamingos Creek by night and day.

Interrogate the inhabitants and be careful with the town by night… the Ovnifagos will be after you!

Fish an ancestral coelacanth, wake up a giant dinosaur made of avocados and discover a new type of “refreshing” tobacco.

Discover in Baobabs Mausoleum an unparalleled adventure, a mad world you will never forget.

¿Did I mention that Watracio is a vampire eggplant?

Terror and mysterious characters awaits you… Welcome to Flamingos Creek: Population 64.

Baobabs Mausoleum Ep.2: 1313 Barnabas Dead End Drive is the second chapter of the complete adventure.

Available FIRST chapter on Steam:

reviews.review:
"Baobabs Mausoleum Ep.2: 1313 Barnabas Dead End Drive" is a 2D pixelcrap game made for the Nintendo Switch (the Nintendo Switch can do primitive 3D graphics so there's no excuses for the laziness here) where you control what looks like a 12 year old's attempt at interactive fiction... a vampire who works for the FBI, to solve a mystery about dinosaurs.  I correct that, 10 year old attempt at interactive fiction.
 
 Gameplay is basically "I can't believe it's not an RPG Maker asset flip" JRPG with all the roleplaying and combat removed... yep, a crap "adventure" game where you RPG Maker move around environments, and click through badly written dialogue with the NPCs.  This is pretty awful... but at least it's not AI slop or an asset flip?  Just because a game is genuinely and ethically made, doesn't mean it's good.
 
And yes, it doesn't matter which sequence it launched on which platforms, this was designed for the lowest common denominator... it's a Switch game.

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.

The amateur pixelcrap visual presentation here at best could have been an attempt to use "retro" as a crutch, a weak excuse to avoid admitting the developer wasn't capable of doing the job of a game developer this decade and creating cutting edge, high quality 3D visuals. While a lack of skill or funding is the explanation for this failure, it's no excuse.  The end result of this incompetence is a game that looks dramatically inferior to professionally developed games.  Terraria and Undertale succeeded [i]despite[/i] looking crap, not [i]because[/i] they look crap.

There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.

The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

To make matters worse, there's no mouse input, despite this being sold on PC as if it were a PC game.  This is unacceptable and somewhat insulting to PC gamers.  It's a good demonstration of the poor attitude the developer has towards PC gamers, and this attitude has resulted in yet another defect in this game.

Those technical flaws drag this game well below the minimum quality standards expected of a modern PC game.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was [b]only 10 players[/b].  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 130 million gamers on Steam and well over 175,000+ games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

Next is pricing and value.  Is this game worth buying from among the 175,000+ games on Steam?

Baobabs Mausoleum Ep.2: 1313 Barnabas Dead End Drive has the far too high price of around $6 USD, it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.

For comparison, the $6 asking price for this game could get you games like "The Elder Scrolls Online", "Subnautica" or "7 Days to Die".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  No pixelcrap is worth $6. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly.

The quality problems and defects with this game makes the asking price totally unrealistic. It's impossible to recommend this to gamers here on Steam.

At the end of the day, my reviews are intended to try help gamers find quality and avoid the dregs (with over 175,000+ games on Steam... not all of them are masterpieces).  If you think my review is wrong, definitely buy this, download it and play it... it's surely exactly the kind of game you'll love (but I doubt it will work out that way).  Game reviews are for gamers to share their thoughts about games and help gamers choose where to spend valuable time or money.   If my review helps you to grab or reject this game, then my job is done.
